pages: Credit Risk Modeling on AWS Real-Time Application Credit Scoring What This Guide Covers: • Real-time credit scoring on AWS • WOE Logistic Regression scorecard • SageMaker Local Mode for model training • LocalStack for local AWS development and testing • CloudFormation for credit scorecard deployment November 2025

Overview This chapter demonstrates a cloud-native credit scoring system using AWS services, imple- mented locally with LocalStack for development and testing. The architecture processes loan applications in real-time, applies a scorecard model, and stores approved applications for au- ditability. Key Learning Objectives By the end of this guide chapter, you will understand: • How nativeAWS services can help in building a credit scoring system • Weight of Evidence (WOE) transformation for credit risk modeling • Selecting optimal cutoff for credit decisioning • Local development workflow using LocalStack and SageMaker Local Mode • Infrastructure as Code (IaC) with CloudFormation templates for deployment Architecture Components The credit scoring system consists of two main flows: Training and Inference. Training Flow Model Training Pipeline The training pipeline implements a credit scorecard using Weight of Evidence (WOE) trans- formation combined with logistic regression: 1. Data Preparation: Historical credit data stored in S3 (training data bucket) 2. Model Training: SageMaker trains a WOE + Logistic Regression pipeline 3. Scorecard Conversion: Logistic coefficients are converted to a points-based scorecard using the standard credit scoring convention 4. Model Artifacts: Trained model and metadata aresaved to S3 (model artifacts store) Scorecard Formula: Score = offset + factor × (β0 + β1 · WOE1 + β2 · WOE2 + . . .) Where: • factor = pts_double_odds ln(2) = 20 ln(2) ≈ 28.85 • offset = target_score − factor × ln(target_odds) = 600− 28.85× ln(30) • Target score: 600, Target odds: 30, Points to double odds: 20 1

Inference Flow Real-Time Scoring Pipeline The inference pipeline processes loan applications in real-time: 1. User: Submits loan application (amount, income, credit history, etc.) 2. Kinesis Data Stream: Ingests application data as streaming events 3. Lambda Function: • Triggered by Kinesis events • Loads trained scorecard model from S3 • Applies WOE transformation and calculates credit score • Compares score against cutoff (502 points) 4. DynamoDB: Stores approved applications (score ≥ 502) for audit and analysis Decision Logic: Decision = { APPROVED if Score ≥ 502 DECLINED if Score < 502 Credit Scorecard Methodology Weight of Evidence (WOE) Transformation WOE is a powerful technique for transforming categorical and continuous variables in credit scoring: Definition: WOEi = ln ( % of Badsi % of Goodsi ) Alternatively, we can calculate it as WOEi = ln ( % of Goodsi % of Badsi ) thus reversing the sign of the WOE. Why use WOE in application credit scoring? • Economic relationships: Establishes monotonic relationships with log-odds of default • Handles missing and special values: Can assign WOE to missing and special categories • Interpretability: Positive WOE indicates higher risk of default, negative WOE indicates lower risk of default Pipeline: Raw Features WOE Transform −−−−−−−−−→ WOE Values Logistic Regression −−−−−−−−−−−→ Log-Odds Scorecard −−−−−−→ Credit Score 2

Optimal Cutoff Determination The cutoff is determined by maximizing the separation between goods and bads using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov Statistic (also Youden Index): Strategy: Find threshold where difference between % bads captured and % goods cap- tured is maximum: Cutoff∗ = arg max threshold ( Sharebads(threshold)− Sharegoods(threshold) ) For our trained model: • Optimal cutoff: 502 points • Approval rate: ∼60% • Bad rate in approved: ∼15% • Gini coefficient: 0.5847 (strong discriminatory power) Local Development with LocalStack Why LocalStack? LocalStack enables local AWS development without cloud costs or internet dependency: • Cost-effective: No AWS charges during development • Fast iteration: Instant deployment and testing • Reproducible: Consistent environment across team members • Offline development: Works without internet connection • CI/CD friendly: Easy integration with automated testing Services Emulated: • S3 (training data and model storage) • Kinesis Data Streams (real-time ingestion) • Lambda (scoring logic) • DynamoDB (approved applications storage) • CloudFormation (infrastructure deployment) LocalStack includes a number of services that are not available in the AWS Free Tier, such as Kinesis Data Streams and DynamoDB. For SageMaker, we are using the Local Mode which is a Docker container that simulates the AWS SageMaker environment without cloud costs. Code Examples Training with SageMaker Python SDK This example shows how to use SageMaker’s Local Mode to train a model in a Docker container on your local machine, simulating the AWS SageMaker environment without cloud costs. 3

from sagemaker.local import LocalSession from sagemaker.sklearn.estimator import SKLearn # Use LocalSession for local training sagemaker_session = LocalSession() sagemaker_session.config = {'local': {'local_code': True}} # Define the estimator sklearn_estimator = SKLearn( entry_point='train.py', source_dir='training', role='arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/SageMakerRole', instance_type='local', framework_version='1.2-1', py_version='py3', sagemaker_session=sagemaker_session, hyperparameters={ 'target_score': 600, 'target_odds': 30, 'pts_double_odds': 20 } ) # Train the model locally sklearn_estimator.fit({'training': 's3://bucket/data'}) Credit Scorecard Training Script This example shows how to train a credit scorecard model using FastWoe for Weight of Evi- dence transformation and scikit-learn’s Logistic Regression. The pipeline is then converted to a points-based scorecard using the standard credit scoring formula. import numpy as np import pandas as pd from fastwoe import FastWoe from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline # Load credit data df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_example.csv') X = df.drop('Good_Bad', axis=1) y = df['Good_Bad'] # Create WOE + Logistic Regression pipeline pipeline = Pipeline([ ('woe', FastWoe()), ('logistic', LogisticRegression(penalty=None, solver='lbfgs')) ]) # Train the model pipeline.fit(X, y) # Convert to scorecard target_score = 600 target_odds = 30 pts_double_odds = 20 4

factor = pts_double_odds / np.log(2) offset = target_score - factor * np.log(target_odds) # Calculate scores scores = offset - factor * pipeline.decision_function(X) Real-Time Scoring with Lambda This Lambda function is triggered by Kinesis events (a service for real-time streaming data), loads the trained scorecard pipeline, calculates credit scores for incoming applications, and stores approved applications (score ≥ cutoff) in DynamoDB, a key-value store for storing ap- proved applications. import json import boto3 import joblib # Load trained model pipeline = joblib.load('model/scorecard_pipeline.joblib') metadata = json.load(open('model/scorecard_metadata.json')) def lambda_handler(event, context): # Parse Kinesis record for record in event['Records']: payload = json.loads(base64.b64decode(record['kinesis']['data'])) # Extract features features = pd.DataFrame([{ 'loan_amount': payload['amount'], 'income': payload['income'], 'debt_to_income': payload['dti'], # ... other features }]) # Calculate credit score score = calculate_score(features, pipeline, metadata) # Decision logic if score >= metadata['cutoff']: store_approved_application(payload, score) return {'decision': 'APPROVED', 'score': score} else: return {'decision': 'DECLINED', 'score': score} 5

Sending Applications to Kinesis Next, we pass loan applications to the Kinesis stream for real-time processing. Each application includes loan amount, income, debt-to-income ratio, and other application features. import json from datetime import datetime import boto3 kinesis = boto3.client('kinesis', endpoint_url='http://localhost:4566') # Generate loan application application = { 'application_id': f'app-{datetime.now().timestamp()}', 'amount': 25000, 'income': 65000, 'debt_to_income': 0.35, 'credit_history_length': 5, 'num_credit_lines': 3, 'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat() } # Send to Kinesis response = kinesis.put_record( StreamName='credit-scoring-stream', Data=json.dumps(application), PartitionKey=application['application_id'] ) print(f"Sent application {application['application_id']}") Querying Approved Applications In this step, we query the DynamoDB table for approved applications. import boto3 dynamodb = boto3.resource('dynamodb', endpoint_url='http://localhost:4566') table = dynamodb.Table('ApprovedApplications') # Scan approved applications response = table.scan() for item in response['Items']: print(f"ID: {item['application_id']}") print(f"Score: {item['credit_score']}") print(f"Amount: ${item['loan_amount']:,.0f}") print(f"Income: ${item['income']:,.0f}") print(f"Timestamp: {item['timestamp']}") 6
